findings.text: PROTOCOL section 7 P1 and RESULTS ('because the 9-target rho mean was high') state the 9-target Q mean was about 14% above sqrt(pi r/2). The 18 Q rows at k = 0..2 (lean-rho study) give 1.0009 (ratio of means) and 0.976 (mean of per-run ratios). The premise is unsupported; the conclusion drawn from it ('the old ratio was not a product of an unlucky rho sample') is consistent with the data. Needs an ERRATA.md line (PROTOCOL.md is frozen).

benchmarks/records/20261118T0710Z-genus4-followup.json metric w_over_plain_rho_q3_w1_p16411 says 1.6046 [1.4069, 1.8371]; analysis.json and the validator's recompute give 1.6053 [1.4070, 1.8373]. No computation tried reproduces 1.6046. The record is also still open (status open, closed_utc null, commit_dirty true, raw uploaded false, reports empty).

Q4 charges rho one partition hash and two coefficient additions per step, but the IC walk performs the same per-step work (genus_ladder.rs lines 1508-1512 at ae36cdc6e4: mix64 of the key and two addm per step) and is not charged for it. Charging it as 3 x trials moves arm x Q4 w=1 from 0.2185 to 0.2197 and w=0.1 from 0.0683 to 0.0687; no verdict changes. Q3 is symmetric (neither side charged).

'Below rho at w = 1' holds only against the measured plain rho Q, and in Q3 only at Monte Carlo margin: upper end 0.99960 at the frozen seed, 0.99946 with an interleaved (targets-then-seeds, drawn per target) resampling order, 0.99962 with interpolated quantiles, below 1 for 18 of 50 seeds. Q4 is robust (0.218 [0.192, 0.250]). Against the strongest available reference, negation (the curves' only F_p-automorphisms are the identity and the hyperelliptic involution), the ideal floor sqrt(pi r/4) puts arm x at 0.0022 / 0.126 / 1.240 at w = 0 / 0.1 / 1: the order does not hold across the band, so arm x is not ranked against negation rho. RESULTS.md states the fragility and the 1.24x distance correctly.

resume.sh's statement that it was written before any Q row was read is not verifiable from git (the rows were on disk, uncommitted). Consistent with it: the 2 re-computed keys equal the first run in every field, and the validator replay of a resumed-block key (2640, k=9) is identical.
RESULTS headline row 'w = 0.1, measured rho 0.089' does not name the reading; it is Q3 (Q4 gives 0.068).

The pooled ratio depends on the curve mix. Arm x's cost hardly depends on r (coefficient of variation 1.2% over the 108 keys) while rho scales as sqrt(r). Per curve at w = 1, arm x / sqrt(pi r/2) is 0.998 (172, h = 2), 0.998 (180, h = 2) and 0.707 (2640, h = 1); against the negation floor 1.412, 1.412 and 1.000; against measured Q (Q3) 1.150, 0.907 and 0.685. 'Below plain rho at w = 1' therefore rests on the one prime-order Jacobian; on the two h = 2 curves arm x is at parity with the plain-rho expectation. RESULTS gives h and r per curve but not this decomposition; the preregistered curve-level bootstrap [0.671, 1.150] reflects it.

rho_reference_assessment.measured_reference: plain rho Q is the cheapest measured rho on these curves: on the 18 keys at k = 0..2 the measured negation walk B costs 1.36 / 1.89 / 6.64 x Q (Q3) and 2.64 x Q at w = 1 (Q4); B's steps are 1.85 x sqrt(pi r/4) with 3.00 compares per step. Q's steps are 1.0036 x sqrt(pi r/2). Q does no canonicalisation (PointClasses::trivial), so pricing its C at 0 is right; its 'native' field is only the one-per-step floor.
rho_reference_assessment.strongest_reference: negation (A = 2): validator scan finds no F_p-automorphism of y^2 = f besides the identity and the hyperelliptic involution on any of the 3 curves (affine maps and maps swapping infinity with a rational root; positive controls detect planted ones); Frobenius is the identity on J(F_p). VALIDATION.json uses the ideal floor sqrt(pi r/4) with nothing charged, the strongest reference.
